Weak damping in coupled oscillator chains

A. Sorensen1 and K. Mbeki2
Abstract. We study a chain of N identical oscillators and show that weak damping produces a slow decay rate that scales with the inverse of N2.

Consider the displacement xi of the i-th oscillator, obeying the equation of motion below [3]. The coupling constant k is assumed uniform, and damping enters only through the friction coefficient γ.

ẍi + γẋi = k(xi+1 − 2xi + xi−1)

The eigenfrequencies follow from a standard Fourier ansatz, giving ω2 = 4k sin2(q/2) for each wave number q. Lower modes therefore decay slowly, which explains the long ringing observed in the experiment [5].
